title: SYSK Selects: Polyamory: When two just won't do
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode on polyamory. The hosts define polyamory as a form of consensual, multi-person committed relationship, distinguish it from cheating, swinging, polygamy and open relationships, and discuss evolutionary theories of monogamy in mammals and primates. They cover benefits (emotional and practical support, needs met by multiple partners), how polyamorous relationships work (communication, handling jealousy, hierarchical versus egalitarian structures, veto power, rules, STI testing and body-fluid monogamy), compersion, research by Terri Conley and others, demographics, legal risks to children and custody, and history including the Oneida Commune. The episode ends with a listener mail about tea, specifically pu-erh.
rerun_of: Polyamory: When Two Just Won't Do

segments.title: Opening and defining polyamory
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode and define polyamory as a committed multi-person relationship that differs from cheating, swinging, polygamy and promiscuity, with all partners aware and consenting. They mention Dan Savage's term monogamish.

segments.title: Evolutionary theories of monogamy
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why monogamy is rare among mammals (about five percent of species) and summarize three theories: males guarding offspring from infanticidal rivals, low female density forcing males to stay and guard paternity, and lesser males using parental care to attract females.

segments.title: Benefits of polyamory
segments.summary: The hosts describe benefits including emotional support, a larger support network, sexual connection, and the ability to meet different needs and interests through several partners, with an example from a more than two website account.

segments.title: How polyamorous relationships work: communication and jealousy
segments.summary: The hosts describe the need for strong communication and honesty, and how polyamorous people handle jealousy by examining its underlying assumptions. They cite research by Terri Conley finding jealousy lower in polyamorous and open groups, and sexual satisfaction comparisons, and distinguish open relationships from closed polyamorous groups.

segments.title: Sexual health, rules and structures
segments.summary: The hosts discuss regular STI testing and openness about results in polyamorous groups, a study on cheaters' risky behavior, and ground rules. They describe hierarchical structures with primary, secondary and tertiary partners and equal-weighted groups, veto power, and body-fluid monogamy.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Brief ad break before the second half.

segments.title: Compersion, demographics and the unicorn hunt
segments.summary: The hosts define compersion as happiness at a partner's happiness with someone else, and discuss the research on longevity of polyamorous couples. They describe demographics from Elizabeth Sheff's sociological interviews and the term hunting the unicorn for seeking a bisexual woman.

segments.title: Social acceptance, custody risks and history
segments.summary: The hosts discuss low social acceptance and secrecy, a custody case involving a polyamorous family from an MTV show where the grandmother sued, the lack of research on children raised polyamorously, and survey data on willingness to try non-monogamy. They cover the history of the Oneida Commune and its link to Oneida silverware.

segments.title: Listener mail on pu-erh tea
segments.summary: A listener writes that the show left out pu-erh, a fermented Chinese tea that can be aged for years, and the hosts close the mail segment.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts give social media and contact information and sign off.
